channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Albania: Fire at Education Ministry as students protest
item.description: Riot police deployed in the Albanian capital Tirana on the second day of student protests. The sudden outbreak seemed at least somewhat reminiscent of the widespread demos in France courting international attention.

item.title: [DW] Police raid the major pro-opposition Halk TV channel in Turkey
item.description: Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of an important pro-opposition television station on Wednesdazy, the day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was set to start his defense against corruption charges.

item.title: [DW] EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget
item.description: EU leaders meeting in Brussels will examine measures to curb the bloc's huge trade deficit with China. But they will also be looking to further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of some major elections next year.

item.title: [DW] Romania: 2 ships on fire in Black Sea, 7 crew missing
item.description: Two chemical tankers have caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace.

item.title: [EU Observer] My mixed emotions on the French riots: Yes, fuck Louis Vuitton, but let’s be strategic
item.description: I felt sorry for police facing Molotov cocktails and cobble stones, but also angry about its use of weapons that left young people maimed.

item.title: [DW] France: Young voters blase about Glucksmann's Socialists
item.description: Raphael Glucksmann wants to lead France's Socialists to power without working with the left-populist Jean-Luc Melenchon, who is particularly popular with young voters. How can the center-left candidate win them over?

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe can’t lead on nature at COP17 while cutting biodiversity cash at home
item.description: Europe's leadership at the COP17 in Yerevan next week will depend not only on what we defend in the negotiations, but also on what we are able to implement and finance at home.

item.title: [DW] How reliant is Ukraine on the US-controlled Starlink internet service?
item.description: Kyiv keeps issuing warnings that the satellite internet system Starlink is being restricted in Ukraine. How dependent is the country on the system, and what would happen if it went down?

item.title: [DW] Populist Czech PM Babis goes empty-handed in Senate elections
item.description: Opposition parties still control the Czech Senate, in a major blow to Prime Minister Andrej Babis' and his governing coalition.

item.title: [DW] Russia wants blackout in Ukraine as winter comes — Zelenskyy
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy says Russia is trying to cut electricity and heating to civilians ahead of winter. He also called the US president's waiver of new sanctions on Moscow a boost for Vladimir Putin.

item.title: [EU Observer] UK–EU relations are being reset. British musicians touring Europe must be part of the deal
item.description: The UK government has once again put touring in Europe on the agenda. As London and Brussels rebuild their relationship, cultural mobility should be treated as part of the economic infrastructure, rather than as an afterthought.

item.title: [DW] France: Protesters clash with police in nationwide protests, amid rising social polarization
item.description: Unrest broke out in parts of France as students, trade unionists and Yellow Vest activists took to the streets to protest high prices and inequality. Police arrested over 1,000 people amid chaotic scenes.

item.title: [Financial Times] France’s riots expose the impotence of its political class
item.description: Shocking violence highlights deepening social division, fiscal constraints and a crisis of leadership

item.title: [Euractiv] Military mobility: What to watch out for in Strasbourg trilogue
item.description: The Commission wants the negotiations to wrap before the end of the year

item.title: [Financial Times] US prosecutors allege Saudi royal links in OpenAI bugging case
item.description: Prosecutors argue Abdulrahman Alfozan should continue to be detained in the US due to his ‘considerable support from a foreign government’

item.title: [Politico Europe] After looting spree, France tells online resellers to crack down on traffic of stolen goods
item.description: The French government wants Vinted, Amazon, eBay, Meta and TikTok to work closely with police to stop the sale of stolen goods.

item.title: [EU Observer] The forgotten protests: empty shelves and blocked roads in southern Italy, ignored by the media, reveal neglect by Meloni and EU
item.description: Empty shelves and too-expensive fuel stocks are the last drop in a sea of negligence faced by southern Italians every day. Life at Europe's edges has left many feeling failed by their government, while EU policies could be making things worse.

item.title: [Euractiv] All roads lead to Rome
item.description: Also, in tonight's edition: EPP leadership race gets crowded

item.title: [Financial Times] Saudi Arabia to postpone ‘Davos in the desert’ after Houthi attacks
item.description: Flagship Future Investment Initiative was scheduled to begin next week in Riyadh but will now take place next year

item.title: [Politico Europe] Empêtré dans la crise sécuritaire, le gouvernement n’arrive pas à sortir de la nasse.
item.description: Présenté par GSK.

item.title: [Euractiv] Council eyes tighter control over ‘made-in-Europe’ policy
item.description: Capitals want evidence before Brussels excludes trading partners from perks meant for local manufacturers

item.title: [Euractiv] Conservatives rally to delay EU climate levy on fuels
item.description: Alliance within European People's Party say energy crisis has pushed prices too high already

item.title: [Euractiv] Hungary to ditch food price cap opposed by EU
item.description: The country's grip over supermarket prices has long irked Brussels

item.title: [EU Observer] Russia’s KOSMOS military satellite stalks Finnish spy satellite, in what could see the first strike in a Ukraine star wars (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,698)
item.description: Ukraine is also scrambling to restore drone strikes after sudden Starlink limits and to repel Russian infiltrators in Dobropillia.

item.title: [Euractiv] Putin, Xi and Trump could meet at APEC summit
item.description: Putin has repeatedly ruled out meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy until after a final peace deal is ready

item.title: [Euractiv] Finland plans €100 million deal for one million anti-personnel mines
item.description: Helsinky targets domestic mine production by 2028 after leaving the Ottawa Convention.

item.title: [Euractiv] Berlin coalition talks hit bumps over Left’s alleged criminal ties
item.description: Twenty Social Democrat MPs have criticised the Left party’s stance on antisemitism, organised crime and terrorism

item.title: [Financial Times] Violent protests multiply across Europe
item.description: Looting and clashes with police take place in Milan, Brussels, Liège and Tirana

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK and Poland accuse Hegseth of downplaying allies’ role in Afghanistan
item.description: British leader Andy Burnham's spokesperson says it's "wrong" for the U.S. defense secretary to diminish the importance of NATO countries.

item.title: [Euractiv] Rare disease patients pin hopes on Biotech Act for new treatments
item.description: Ireland aims to conclude the clinical trials section of the legislation this year

item.title: [Euractiv] Commission suspects US fund negligence in Italian telecom deal
item.description: Wholesale access price increased since the merger, telecom operators complained

item.title: [Politico Europe] French PM orders ‘localized’ curfews in response to looting and unrest
item.description: The government faces criticism it failed to adequately prepare for the violence that played out alongside mass protests.

item.title: [Financial Times] US defence stocks tumble as investors bet on Democratic election sweep
item.description: Donald Trump’s proposed $500bn military spending boost at risk as bipartisan support for higher budget frays

item.title: [EU Observer] Trump, Rubio and Hegseth are fumbling Ukraine – Europe needs to stop making the same mistake
item.description: For now, Ukrainians are Europe’s human shields. If their defence breaks, a triumphant, battle-hardened Russia will seek its next victim, while the US may decide to back a winner not a loser. For now, Europe’s problem is only a lack of will-power: a nice problem to have.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU eyes buying new icebreakers as Russia bolsters role in the Arctic
item.description: Icebreakers are traditionally civilian vessels, but they can support military operations by opening sea lanes

item.title: [Euractiv] First Council compromise on EU telecoms law clarifies rules for Big Tech
item.description: But draft document does not touch on copper switch-off or spectrum licences

item.title: [Politico Europe] The multiple sclerosis gap Europe cannot afford to ignore
item.description: Providing the right support and treatment starts with measurement. Current tools do not reflect the lived reality of MS patients and miss early signs of progression.

item.title: [Euractiv] A dozen MEPs battle for 10 top EPP jobs
item.description: Manfred Weber’s dream of a quiet contest won't come true

item.title: [Politico Europe] Adipositas: Sparen kann für den Staat teuer werden
item.description: Adipositas wird in Deutschland vor allem als medizinisches oder individuelles Problem diskutiert. Doch die Erkrankung hat erhebliche wirtschaftliche Folgen. Der Blick ins Ausland zeigt, dass die politische Debatte über die Versorgung von Adipositas auch anders geführt werden kann.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU Inc heads for potential Council deal
item.description: Countries could give thumbs up to draft position on Friday

item.title: [Financial Times] French bond sell-off intensifies after violent protests
item.description: Authorities introduce partial curfews and admit that police botched oversight of protests

item.title: [Euractiv] Ukraine says it evacuated a wounded soldier with a heavy-lift drone
item.description: Kyiv claims it's the first time this has ever been done

item.title: [Financial Times] Zelenskyy, Europe and the end of Trump whispering
item.description: This new crisis looks different and the bloc’s leaders are preparing to talk directly to Putin

item.title: [Financial Times] Freshfields apologises ‘unreservedly’ over Middle East comments in email leak
item.description: Partner at firm had said need to approach ‘sophisticated investors’ to back its AI lab ‘probably’ ruled out region’s ‘sovereign wealth money’

item.title: [Financial Times] CME plans tungsten futures as demand for weapons rises
item.description: China has restricted exports of critical mineral used in armour-piercing munitions

item.title: [Politico Europe] Serbian prosecutor probing Trump Tower in Belgrade targeted with spyware
item.description: The revelations come amid mounting controversy over plans to redevelop the former Yugoslav military headquarters in Belgrade into a new luxury Trump Tower.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU eyes Rome for 2027 summit ahead of Italian election
item.description: Hosting EU leaders in Rome would give Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni a high-profile international stage in an election year.

item.title: [Politico Europe] France riots: Presidential hopeful Attal pitches social media blackout
item.description: The former PM said measures must be “temporary” and “limited to the area where the riots are taking place.”

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s new Franco-German auto pact will protect combustion engines, not European jobs
item.description: Friedrich Merz wanted more time for combustion-engine cars. Emmanuel Macron wanted tougher rules on what qualifies as “Made in Europe.” Now, the two countries have traded one for the other. Both can claim victory at home, and both say they want the same thing: to strengthen Europe’s auto industry against Chinese competition. But the trade-off undermines that very goal.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Where’s Burnham really on welfare reform?
item.description: Having more than a million young people not in education, employment or training is an “economic catastrophe” according to the prime minister. So, what will the government do about it? With Alan Milburn’s long-awaited review due next month, is Andy Burnham laying the groundwork for tougher benefit conditions in the budget – as ministers look […]

item.title: [DW] What Earth's sixth mass extinction event means for humans
item.description: Human activity is driving plants and animals to extinction at an unprecedented rate. As countries meet in Armenia to discuss ways to reverse nature loss, DW reveals how declining biodiversity is already harming people.

item.title: [Financial Times] ‘I suffer with my wallet’: American voters weigh in on the midterms
item.description: The FT’s focus group in the Pennsylvania battleground of Bethlehem revealed anxiety about the country ahead of November’s elections

item.title: [EU Observer] THIS WEEK: Budget fallout, Russian provocations, and could the ICC be awarded the EU’s Sakharov prize?
item.description: MEPs in Strasbourg will respond to Donald Trump's sanctions against the International Criminal Court, debate Russian drones in the Black Sea and decide positions on short- and long-term budgets.

item.title: [DW] Ukrainian President Zelenskyy speaks at EU summit amid spat with Donald Trump
item.description: EU leaders reaffirmed support for Ukraine at the Brussels summit. But souring relations with the US over Russia and Starlink and a big hole in the budget will make for a difficult winter for Ukraine.

item.title: [EU Observer] Denmark lashes out again at Sánchez over Spain’s migration regularisation, but EU summit avoids linking migration to crime
item.description: Danish prime minister Mette Frederiksen lashed out again at Spanish leader Pedro Sánchez on migration during a summit debate in Brussels on Friday.

item.title: [DW] Hijab ban at schools in Azerbaijan: What's behind the rare wave of protests?
item.description: Girls wearing headscarves have been turned away from schools in Azerbaijan, triggering unusual protests involving children. The government rules do not mention hijabs. Why are schools enforcing unwritten rules?

item.title: [EU Observer] US-Russia ‘diesel deal’ could open door to wider sanctions relief, Zelensky warns as EU vows to keep supporting Ukraine
item.description: Volodomyr Zelensky flew into Brussels warning that Washington’s surprise ‘diesel deal’ with Moscow risks becoming the thin end of a wider sanctions rollback - just as Ukraine faces a brutal winter, dwindling air defences and a fresh scramble in EU capitals over money, missiles and frozen Russian billions.

item.title: [EU Observer] Germany and France want own ‘Made in Europe’ rules for cars, outside EU industrial policy
item.description: France and Germany want the rules for cars carved out of the EU's Industrial Accelerator Act and moved into a separate automotive package. Their joint paper also spells out how emissions targets will be weakened.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russian air force suffers worst day since Operation Spiderweb, as Ukraine destroys Su-34 strike aircraft on the ground (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,695)
item.description: While Washington quietly orders Starlink’s military network throttled and Moscow steps up long-range attacks, Ukrainian forces are still capable of audacious success.

item.title: [DW] Albania: Students demand political change and resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama
item.description: Empty lecture halls, burning buildings and demands for change: Albanian students are spearheading a protest movement that has become the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Edi Rama in years.

item.title: [DW] The EU wants an AI revolution. But on whose terms?
item.description: As the US and China race ahead, the European Union seeks to boost its economy with AI. Can it compete while protecting workers, safety and the climate?

item.title: [EU Observer] 17 EU states confirmed on board for plan to let countries close borders and freeze asylum
item.description: Over a dozen EU member states, along with the EU Commission, discussed migration at a pre-summit breakfast on Friday.

item.title: [DW] Italy cuts air traffic in half amid data transmission issue
item.description: Citing problems with the data transmission network, Italian authorities have drastically reduced the volume of flights in their airspace. The ENAV authority ruled out malicious activity and said flights remained safe.

item.title: [EU Observer] Can the EU survive with far-right leaders running major member states? The answer is worrying
item.description: As the EU enters an unprecedented electoral supercycle, the question is whether it can defend its integrity as the forces challenging it gain influence over its institutions.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Too many lawyers’: the problem with Europe’s human rights NGOs
item.description: Traditionally, human rights NGOs have been staffed mainly by lawyers. This is understandable. But advocacy is becoming less effective because decision makers increasingly see supporting human rights as politically risky.
